title: Entropy diagnostics of coverage imbalance and reweighting in archaeological predictive modelling
description:
Code and derived data for an information-theoretic diagnostic of coverage imbalance in archaeological predictive modelling. Computes the Shannon entropy of the distribution of recorded sites across a partition of covariate space, derives a heuristic observation weight from the normalised surprisal, and tests whether this and standard weights (inverse frequency, density ratio) change the predictions of four frameworks (Random Forest, penalised-spline logistic GAM, MaxEnt in penalised-logistic form, and non-spatial Bayesian logistic regression) under both random and catchment-blocked cross-validation.

The input dataset is the published supplementary data of Yaworsky et al. (2020) for the Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument, archived at tDAR (doi:10.6067/XCV8457626). It contains no coordinates: archaeological site locations in the United States are withheld under statutory protection. All entropy quantities are therefore defined over covariate space rather than geographic space.

Version 1.1 adds the analyses requested during peer review (alternative weights, partition comparisons, blocked-design sensitivity checks, training-fold thresholds and a simulation with a known survey mechanism) and pins package versions.
